description:
## Why

docs/research/nif-workloads.md found that about 47 of the top 50 Rustler packages wrap an existing library, and the same holds for elixir_make packages. Those were set aside as "defk can't help". This epic pushes that line: for the libraries whose reference implementation is plain, portable C-shaped code over bytes and numbers, with a spec and test vectors, an extended defk can plausibly match the wrapper and add what it never had.

## What a from-scratch kernel buys over a wrapper

- Memory safety on untrusted input: every a[i] is bounds-checked or proven in range, every integer op is overflow-checked. A defk decoder cannot buffer-overflow; the worst case is an exception in the caller. For decompressors, image decoders and anything fed network bytes, that is the CVE class that matters.
- The runtime contract: yields every 250 us where the wrapped NIF blocks or runs dirty; a killed process frees its frame; hot upgrade.
- One toolchain (cc) instead of Rust plus precompiled artifacts.
- Elixir mode: readable as Elixir, debuggable, and checked by the agreement property against the reference library's own vectors.

## The honest ceiling

clang without intrinsics. Where the reference is plain C (lz4, snappy, argon2, keccak, inflate) parity is plausible. Where the reference is SIMD-tuned (crc32c, simdutf8, zstd, brotli, libjpeg-turbo, libvips) a kernel will be slower, and the entry says so and argues safety and yielding instead. Every ticket pre-registers its expected verdict against the best Elixir baseline (the catalog rule: guide, do not exclude; prioritise what defk can make better).

## Tiers

Tier 1 (children 1-6): unlocked by the extensions the text work already ticketed (defk-w38, defk-n4r.2, defk-ivt, defk-n4r.4), plus one small builtin ticket here. Tier 2 (children 7-13): each needs one or two further constructs (defk-cmr bitstring accumulator or two-pass output, defk-4ai narrow types, defk-6ag code-size guard). Tier 3, kernel-owned state across calls, is its own epic (see the sibling epic), because it is a semantics change, not a construct.

## Not worth rewriting

Recorded, with the reasons and what would change each, in the "Document the rewrite boundary" child; the short form: signing and key exchange (no constant-time guarantee from a C-emitting compiler), parsers that produce trees (term creation is the cost and the product), regex (:re is PCRE in C), large codecs and encoders with big spec surfaces (brotli, zstd encode, audio, video), and systems (SQLite, DuckDB, Polars, XLA), where the value is the library.

## Sequencing

```mermaid
graph LR
  w38[defk-w38 bitwise] --> t1[Tier 1: keccak, blake, lz4/snappy decode, geohash/crc]
  n4r2[defk-n4r.2 word loads] --> t1
  ivt[defk-ivt constants] --> t1
  n4r4[defk-n4r.4 writable helpers] --> t1
  fft[FFT/convolution: ready now]
  img[image resize/convert: ready now]
  t1 --> bits[mulhi/clz/popcount builtins]
  cmr[defk-cmr growable output] --> inflate[inflate + PNG]
  t1 --> inflate
  inflate --> zstd[zstd decode]
  inflate --> jpeg[baseline JPEG]
  t1 --> argon[argon2id] --> bcrypt
  n4r6[defk-n4r.6 hash table pattern] --> lz4enc[lz4/snappy encode]
```

Done when: every child has a measured verdict or a recorded reason it was not built, and the rewrite boundary is in the docs.

comments.text: Deferred 2026-10-13 (focus review): expansion work waits until the verdict closes (defk-sgw.6). The date is a placeholder; the trigger is defk-sgw.6 closing. Nothing is dropped: bw ready hides deferred issues, bw list --all shows them.

title: From-scratch kernels where people wrap a library in a NIF today
